concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of a swelling and discharging pus on the right upper eyelid, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, are consistent with a frontal sinus mucocele.
The patient's 2-year history of swelling and discharge, along with imaging findings of opacification and inflammatory infiltrate, suggest a chronic infection of the frontal sinus.

The patient's symptoms of a swelling and discharging pus on the right upper eyelid, combined with imaging findings of ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, could be consistent with orbital cellulitis.

The patient's symptoms of a swelling and discharge on the right upper eyelid, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, suggest a sinusitis with orbital complication.
The patient's symptoms of a discharging pus on the right upper eyelid, combined with imaging findings of opacification and inflammatory infiltrate, could be consistent with a pyocele.
